sector: Industrial O&M services, project execution and metal fabrication (metals, ports, cement)

company_pe.pat_basis: restated consolidated; all attributable to owners
company_pe.source: RHP pp. 134-136 (Basis for Issue Price); PAT p. 86
company_pe.note: EPS is on 6.745 crore weighted shares after the 6:1 bonus (May-2025) and the Jul-2025 placement. On the 6.904 crore pre-issue shares FY26 EPS is Rs 3.75 (P/E 17.3x at Rs 65); on the 9.604 crore post-issue shares it is Rs 2.70 (P/E 24.1x). The industry P/E (48.66 / 5.99 / 27.32) is as printed on p. 135 and includes Thermax. Band as announced by the company and reported (Kotak Neo, Chittorgarh); the RHP prints [●].

business_stage: Scaling (O&M share up from 64% to 80% of revenue FY24-26; order book 3.1x revenue; port O&M added from FY25)

anchor.source: Anchor bidding 1-Dec-2026; allocation not yet published at writing

headline: A Chittorgarh industrial O&M and erection contractor for metal smelters, mines, ports and cement plants (FY26 revenue Rs 562 cr, EBITDA margin 8.7%, PAT Rs 25.9 cr; Vedanta group 78% of revenue), priced at 24.1x FY26 earnings (28.6x after recurring gratuity losses) against an 18.8x peer median; fair value Rs 47 (Neutral) because thin margins and working capital near 18% of revenue leave little free cash, while the order book and 20%+ ROCE support the business.
red_flags: Vedanta group (incl. Hindustan Zinc) 77.9% of FY26 and 83.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue; Hindustan Zinc alone 35.4% (pp. 27, 190)
Unexecuted order book Rs 1,761.9 cr = 3.1x FY26 revenue, 96% multi-year O&M (p. 189)
Cumulative CFO 67% of PAT FY24-26; FY26 CFO Rs 8.1 cr as receivables rose Rs 33.2 cr (p. 87)
Rs 120 cr of proceeds go to working capital, mainly to cut trade payables from Rs 71.6 cr to Rs 20.0 cr (p. 120)
Band Rs 60-65; fair value Rs 38.6 / 47.2 / 52.2 vs Rs 65; Jul-2025 placement at Rs 38 (p. 103)

strengths: Order book Rs 1,761.9 cr = 3.1x FY26 revenue (p. 189)
16-year relationship with Hindustan Zinc; 87-94% repeat-client revenue (pp. 27, 138)
Owned fleet of 232 cranes, hydras, trucks and excavators (p. 189)
weaknesses: Late PF, ESIC, TDS and GST payments in each period (pp. 35-36)
opportunities: New Vedanta Goa and Silvassa units (p. 441)
Outsourcing of maintenance in metals and cement; O&M market +6% a year (p. 168)
UAE work through Monomark Engineering FZE (p. 191)
threats: Non-renewal or re-pricing of a large Vedanta-group contract
Wage and labour-law cost inflation on a 6,800-person workforce
Recourse on Rs 23.0 cr of receivables financed by SBI for Vedanta (p. 88)

call_basis: Call rule (ROUTINE.md hard rule 6), judged at the upper band of Rs 65 (as announced by the company and reported): Neutral value Rs 47.2 is 27.4% below the price, inside the -10% to -30% band, so the call is Neutral (Bull Rs 52.2 is also below the price, -19.6%). At the Rs 60 floor the Neutral value is 21.3% below. It would read Subscribe at about Rs 52.5 or below and Avoid above about Rs 67.4. No material issue under the Fund's rules.
reference_note: Band Rs 60-65, lot 225 (company announcement as reported; RHP prints [●]). At Rs 65: 9.604 crore post-issue shares, market cap Rs 624 cr; P/E 24.1x FY26 PAT (28.6x on adjusted Rs 21.83 cr); company's own P/E 16.9x (pre-issue weighted shares); P/B 2.24x post-issue; EV/EBITDA 10.6x FY26.
